Body.raw:
Goal: agents emit permalinks into a todo, e.g.
http://localhost:8765/557a/objid/0a3f -- the webserver opens that todo and
navigates to the item at hand.

Two coupled features.

## 1. objid

Every JSON object nested in a todo record carries an immutable, required,
unique-within-the-todo short id: "objid": "0a3f" (lowercase hex, %04x of a
creation-order counter; widens past 4 chars only if a todo ever exceeds 65536
objects). Uniqueness scope is the single todo; a subtodo is a separate scope.
Top-level "_nextobjid" (int) is the allocation cursor.

Ratified decisions:

- EXEMPT: the root object (already addressed by Id), "State", and the state
  value object ("State.done" etc). Stamping State would break doctors
  exactly-one-key check and every _STATE_METADATA allow-list. State stays
  addressable by path without an objid.
- STAMPED: Summary, Body, Scope, Agent, Parent[], Subtodos[], Tag[],
  WorkItems[], WorkItems[].execution -- i.e. every other nested object,
  discovered by walk, not by an enumerated list.
- _nextobjid is NOT an opportunistic lock (struck by the user). update_dt is
  the field that would serve that role if we ever want it.
- Immutability: an existing objid is never rewritten. A duplicate (from an
  object copied within a record) is broken by giving the LATER occurrence a
  fresh id; first occurrence keeps its identity.
- Choke point: stamp in write_todo_worktree beside normalize_todo_schema, so
  all 28 write call sites are covered by one hook. The two direct store.put
  sites (migrate sweep, embedding backfill) write records that are already
  stamped.
- Existing records are stamped by a record migration (SCHEMA_VERSION 8 -> 9,
  RECORD_MIGRATIONS[9]), so doctor sweeps it in via migrate-to-latest.
- _nextobjid joins ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS.

## 2. Permalinks

Path grammar, all path segments (no query string):

  /<todoid>/<segment>...

- <todoid>: 4+ hex Id prefix (same selector rule as everywhere else).
- Collections take a where-clause of exactly two segments, key then value:
  idx, sha, subtodo_id, objid. sha/subtodo_id/objid match on a 4+ prefix;
  idx is an exact integer and is NOT shortenable.
- Indexes are 0-BASED, identical to the json dot-path, jq, and doctor finding
  labels. /workitem/1 translates to WorkItems.1 with no arithmetic, so a link
  an agent emits from jq output cannot be off by one.
- A bare segment in where-clause position is ALWAYS idx (the list default).
  So /557a/workitem/883368/summary is well defined -- index 883368 -- and
  simply out of bounds. There is no bare-hex fallback.
- /<todoid>/objid/<prefix> addresses any object anywhere in the todo, with no
  collection named. This is the canonical permalink form and the one agents
  should emit; the json path form is deliberately not exposed.

Field naming (ratified -- there is NO inflection engine):

- A segment matches a record field name CASE-INSENSITIVELY: workitems,
  WorkItems, scope, oxen, geese all resolve to the field of that name.
- ONE usability aid: for a LIST-valued field whose name ends in "s", the name
  minus that trailing "s" also resolves. This is not singularization -- it is
  naming the element type: WorkItems is a List[WorkItem], so /workitem/ works.
  Oxen is a List[Ox] as far as English is concerned but we do not know that,
  so only /oxen/ works and /ox/ is an error. That is the correct outcome.
  (If a real element-type schema ever lands -- WorkItems: List[WorkItem] --
  this aid should be driven from it and the trailing-s rule dropped.)
- Precedence: an exact case-insensitive field-name match beats a drop-the-s
  alias, so "tag" resolves to Tag, never to legacy Tags.

Examples:
  /557a/workitem/5/summary
  /557a/workitems/5/summary
  /557a/workitem/idx/5/summary
  /557a/workitem/sha/883368/summary
  /557a/workitem/objid/0a3f
  /557a/subtodo/subtodo_id/13e5
  /557a/objid/0a3f

Implementation shape:

- The first step is a pure translation: url path -> internal json dot-path.
  Everything else works from that path, exactly like get-json-path.
- CLI: "todo.py resolveurl <path-or-url>" prints the addressed JSON value.
  It needs no selector -- the todoid is in the path. Accepts a full URL or a
  bare path. No inverse (url-emitting) command: the user does not want the
  json path exposed when objid is available.
- Web: todo_web routes /<todoid>/<rest...>, resolves it, finds the nearest
  enclosing objid-bearing object, and 302-redirects to
  /?id=<todoid>#obj-<objid>. render_todo_page grows id="obj-<objid>" anchors
  on the work-item / subtodo / parent boxes so the browser lands on the item.
  The existing /?id= and /search routes are unchanged.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): objid allocator and stamper core

New module skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo_objid.py: stamp_objids(todo)
gives every nested JSON object in a todo record an immutable, unique-within-
the-todo objid (lowercase hex, %04x from the new top-level _nextobjid cursor,
widening past 4 chars above 65536 objects). iter_objects(todo) yields
(json_path, object) in walk order for later reuse by doctor and the URL
resolver.

Root and the whole State subtree are exempt: the root is already named by Id,
and stamping State would break doctor's exactly-one-key check plus every
_STATE_METADATA allow-list.

Existing ids are never rewritten, so re-stamping is a no-op; an object is
re-issued only when its id is missing, malformed, or duplicates one seen
earlier in the walk (later occurrence loses). _nextobjid is advanced past
every id present, including ids already above the stored cursor.

Nothing is wired into the write path yet -- this is the pure core.

Tests: skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_objid.py, 20 cases covering
stamping coverage, root/State exemption, walk order, immutability across
re-stamp, duplicate reassignment, malformed and uppercase ids, cursor
handling and recovery, 4-hex widening, and iter_objects paths. Full todos
suite green (356 passed); pylint 10.00/10 on both files.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] objid allocator + stamper core: pure _stamp_objids(todo) walking the record, exempting root/State/State.<name>, allocating %04x from _nextobjid, preserving existing ids, re-assigning the later of a duplicate pair. Unit tests for each of those properties.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): stamp objids at the write choke point

Wire todo_objid.stamp_objids into write_todo_worktree, right after
normalize_todo_schema, so all 28 write call sites (and the legacy TODO.json
path) persist objids without any command having to remember. Add _nextobjid
to ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS so doctor accepts the allocation cursor.

Stamping happens on WRITE only, never on read: a read-time stamp would mint
ids that are not persisted and would differ between reads.

The embedding machinery is unaffected -- _is_vector and _inline_embeddings
both require a list-of-lists-of-numbers, so a string objid is never mistaken
for an embedder key in Summary/Body/Tag.

Two existing tests asserted exact work-item dict equality and now see the new
field; both keep their strictness by popping objid and asserting its shape
separately (test_work_item_aliases_add_and_done_items,
test_set_json_path_from_stdin_replaces_work_items).

Tests: new ObjidWiringTests in test_todo.py, 9 cases -- mint and init stamp,
root and State stay unstamped, ids unique within a todo, ids survive an
unrelated edit, a new work item gets a fresh id, _nextobjid stays ahead of
every id, a subtodo is a separate id scope (counter restarts at 0000), and
doctor accepts _nextobjid. Full todos suite green (365 passed).

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): backfill objids via record migration v9

Bump todo_db.SCHEMA_VERSION 8 -> 9 and register RECORD_MIGRATIONS[9] =
migrate_record_v9, which runs todo_objid.stamp_objids over the record. This
is the record axis only -- no table DDL changes -- so existing stores gain
objids through the sweep doctor already runs (migrate-to-latest), with no
command a human has to remember.

Idempotent by construction: stamp_objids never rewrites a well-formed id, so
a swept record re-sweeps to itself and migrate-to-latest reports migrated=0
on the second pass. Hand-seeded ids survive the sweep.

test_todo_migrate.py is the frozen AC for the migrator and is generic over
SCHEMA_VERSION -- unmodified, still green.

Tests: MigrateRecordV9Test in test_todo_objid.py, 4 cases -- legacy record
gains objids and _nextobjid, sweep is idempotent, hand-seeded ids preserved,
version 9 registered. Full todos suite green (369 passed); pylint 10.00/10.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] Record migration: bump SCHEMA_VERSION 8->9, register RECORD_MIGRATIONS[9] stamping legacy records. Tests: legacy record gains objids, migrate-to-latest is idempotent, --dry-run writes nothing.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): doctor hard-fails broken objids

Add objid_findings(todo) beside workitem_findings and wire it into
doctor_findings. A permalink names an object by objid, so a missing,
malformed, or reused id is a broken link rather than cosmetic drift, and
_nextobjid falling behind would hand the next allocation an id already in
use -- silently moving an existing permalink onto a different object. All
four are hard findings (exit 1).

None of these can arise through the CLI: the write choke point re-stamps
anything malformed and doctor's own schema sweep backfills legacy records,
so a finding here means something wrote the store outside todo.py. The CLI
tests therefore corrupt sqlite directly, and only AFTER a first doctor run
has swept the store -- otherwise the opportunistic sweep repairs the damage
before the audit sees it (doctor repairs, then audits).

Tests in test_todo.py: ObjidDoctorTests (3 end-to-end cases -- missing,
duplicate, stale cursor -- each asserting exit 1 and the finding text) and
ObjidFindingUnitTests (8 unit cases: clean record, record with no objects,
missing, malformed, duplicate naming the first holder, cursor behind, cursor
not an integer, State never reported). Full todos suite green (380 passed).
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] doctor checks: hard findings for missing, malformed, or duplicate objid and for a _nextobjid behind the max allocated. Tests per finding, plus a clean record reporting ok.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): permalink path grammar (url path -> json dot-path)

New module skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo_url.py. split_url_path()
splits a full URL or bare path into (todo selector, segments), discarding
scheme/host/query/fragment and percent-decoding. to_json_path() walks those
segments against a record and returns the internal dot-path, which is what
every downstream consumer works from -- one grammar, interpreted once.

Grammar as ratified:
- dict segment: field name matched case-insensitively; ONE aid, a list-valued
  field ending in s also answers to the name minus that s (naming the element
  type, not singularizing -- Oxen answers only to oxen). Exact match beats the
  alias, so tag is Tag even with legacy Tags present.
- list segment: where-clause, default key idx. A bare segment is ALWAYS an
  index, so /workitem/883368/summary is well defined and simply out of bounds.
  Indexes are 0-based, matching the json path, jq and doctor labels exactly.
  sha / subtodo_id / objid match on a 4+ character prefix; ambiguity is an
  error naming the candidates.
- /<todoid>/objid/<prefix> is the canonical collection-free lookup; below the
  root, objid is an ordinary field (the root is never stamped, so nothing is
  shadowed).

Tests: skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_url.py, 36 cases over URL
splitting, case-insensitivity, 0-based and explicit idx, out-of-bounds vs
non-numeric bare segments, drop-the-s on lists only, Tag beating Tags, sha /
subtodo_id / objid prefixes, top-level objid walked further, widened 5-hex
ids, and every error path. pylint 10.00/10.
WorkItems.summary: [HICAP] URL path grammar: pure translator url-path -> internal json dot-path. Segments match field names case-insensitively; a list field ending in s also answers to the name minus that s (element type, not singularization); exact match beats the alias. Indexes 0-based. Table-driven tests: bare idx, explicit idx, out-of-bounds idx, sha/objid/subtodo_id 4+ prefixes, ambiguous prefix error, unknown field error, case-insensitive names, drop-the-s on lists only, Tag over Tags, top-level /objid/<prefix>.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): resolveurl subcommand dereferences a permalink

todo.py resolveurl <path-or-url> prints the value a permalink addresses,
exactly as get-json-path prints it for the equivalent dot-path. It takes no
selector -- the todo IS the first path segment -- and accepts a full URL or a
bare path, so a link pasted out of a browser resolves as-is. Errors from the
grammar surface as TodoError (exit 1) naming the todo they failed in.

There is deliberately no inverse command: the json path is not the handle we
want agents holding. objid is, and /<todoid>/objid/<prefix> is the form to
emit.

Tests: ResolveUrlTests in test_todo.py, 12 cases -- field path, 0-based bare
index, output identical to get-json-path, full URL with host and port, objid
with no collection named, drop-the-s and plural agreeing, tag, todoid-only
printing the record, and the error paths (out of bounds, unknown field,
unknown todo). One case pins the whole point of objids: after work-item-insert
shifts the list, the objid link still resolves to the same work item while the
index link silently means a different one. Full todos suite green (428).
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] todo.py resolveurl <path-or-url> subcommand: accepts full URL or bare path, prints the addressed JSON value. Tests: matches get-json-path output for the equivalent path; error paths exit nonzero.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): viewer serves permalinks and renders objid anchors

todo_web routes /<todoid>/<path...> and 302-redirects onto the anchored page,
/?id=<Id>#obj-<objid>. Redirecting rather than rendering keeps ONE page-render
path: the permalink is the durable name, the ?id= URL is where the browser
ends up. permalink_target() computes that URL and is the unit-testable seam.

A link may address a scalar, but a page can only scroll to a box, so
todo_url.nearest_objid walks up the json path to the innermost stamped object
-- .../workitem/1/summary lands on the work-item box. A path with nothing
stamped above it (the State subtree, or the record itself) lands on the page
with no fragment rather than erroring.

Boxes carry id=obj-<objid> via the new _anchor() helper, fed by objid on the
work-item / subtodo / parent view dicts (taken from THIS record's entry, not
the loaded child). Only INTERACTIVE boxes are anchored: a static rendition in
the fold shows another todo's record, whose objids are a different id scope
and would otherwise emit duplicate DOM ids. A one-line :target CSS rule marks
which box the link landed on.

Routing is gated on a 4+ hex first segment, so /favicon.ico and friends keep
their old 404 instead of being swallowed; /?id= and /search are untouched.

Tests: new test_todo_web_permalink.py, 14 cases -- 7 unit cases on
permalink_target (object path, scalar path, objid form, sha where-clause,
record with no fragment, unstamped subtree, bad path) and 7 against a live
server on an ephemeral port asserting the 302 and Location for object / short
selector / objid links, 404 for an unresolvable path, unknown todo and a
non-permalink path, and /search still 200. Plus PermalinkAnchorTests in
test_todo.py (3 cases: work-item anchor, subtodo anchor, no duplicate anchors
once a static rendition is on the page). Full suite green (445 passed).
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] todo_web: route /<todoid>/<path...> -> 302 to /?id=<todoid>#obj-<objid> at the nearest enclosing objid-bearing object; emit id=obj-<objid> anchors in the work-item/subtodo/parent boxes. Tests: redirect target, anchor presence, /?id= and /search unchanged.
